clue.text: Risk superior cast (the Guardian's) coming in to strip

indicators.note: the cast and the Guardian's piece come into the middle of the word for strip, which then holds them

blocks.note: U means upper-class, superior in social standing
to shy is to throw or cast
the newspaper speaking of itself: belonging to us
to strip a bird of its feathers

explanation.surface: A newspaper puff about its own superior team of writers stripping off, which sounds a risky business.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip means pluck, as a bird of its feathers, and the cast is a throw. Risk is the theme word running through the puzzle's clues.
explanation.definitionFit: To push your luck is to take a further chance after things have gone well, inviting trouble.

clue.text: Duck and fish in case

indicators.note: the fish sits inside the case, which wraps around it

blocks.note: the char is a trout-like freshwater fish
a pod is the case holding peas or seeds

explanation.surface: A shopping list or recipe: a duck and some fish packed in a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck and fish' reads as two things to buy; only the duck is the definition, and 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The pochard is a species of diving duck common on European lakes and reservoirs.

clue.text: Relative of princes' sister accepting old money

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the abbreviation for sister holds the money

blocks.note: pence were the coins of the old pre-decimal British currency
Sr is the standard abbreviation for sister, as in a nun's title

explanation.surface: A royal sister taking a handout, perhaps a family allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: Princes William and Harry's mother was Diana Spencer, so any Spencer of her family is their relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana, Princess of Wales, was born a Spencer, making that aristocratic family kin to her royal sons.

clue.text: Sleep easy, result of being polite?

indicators.note: the letters as given produce a new arrangement as their result

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Good manners as a recipe for a clear conscience and a good night's rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Result' does double duty: it signals the rearrangement and belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying yes please is what courtesy produces when accepting an offer, the polite form of agreement.

clue.text: BBC's leader dismissed and set loose

indicators.note: the first letter of the nickname is sent away, leaving the rest

blocks.note: Auntie is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: The head of the BBC is sacked and freed from his duties.
explanation.walkthrough: The leader is not B, the first letter of BBC, but A, the first letter of the BBC's nickname AUNTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie something is to undo its knots, releasing it so that it is free.

clue.text: Overture, one or other, in US city

indicators.note: the words are made other than they are, that is put in a different order
the rearranged words go inside the abbreviation for the city

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
taken as written

explanation.surface: Choosing between one overture and another for a concert in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One or other' reads as an everyday phrase; 'one or' is the fodder and 'other' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven wrote three overtures named Leonora for his opera Fidelio, so the title names a piece of orchestral music.

clue.text: Aquarium dweller as model provided rise in money

indicators.note: in a down clue a rising word reads from bottom to top, so backwards
the model and the rising word go inside the money

blocks.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
if means on condition that, provided
cash is ready money

explanation.surface: A fish posing for a picture, on condition that its fee goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' is a car here, not a person posing; 'as' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Catfish, whiskered bottom-feeders, are popular tank fish kept to clean the floor of home tanks.

clue.text: Roy's peculiar arrangement thus involving risk

indicators.note: an odd arrangement of the letters puts them in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; it is fodder as well as part of the signal

explanation.surface: Roy has set things out in an odd and dangerous way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peculiar' is both fodder and part of the signal: Roy's peculiar letters are given an arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Precariously means in an unstable, dangerous manner, which 'thus involving risk' describes as an adverb.

clue.text: Complaint involving risk, etc

indicators.note: to involve is to entangle or twist together, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble about all the hazards and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: Complaint here means an illness, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Rickets is a childhood disease softening the bones through lack of vitamin D, and complaint is an old word for ailment.

clue.text: Dance bringing ursine perambulation to a ticklish conclusion?

definitions.text: bringing ursine perambulation to a ticklish conclusion?

blocks.note: first meaning: a ballroom dance in duple time

blocks.clueFragment: bringing ursine perambulation to a ticklish conclusion?
blocks.note: second meaning: the line of a children's tickling rhyme about a teddy bear just before the tickle

explanation.walkthrough: The British nursery rhyme 'Round and round the garden, like a teddy bear' ends 'one step, two step, tickly under there', with a tickle.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a lively ballroom dance, and also the phrase in the rhyme just before the tickling arrives.

clue.text: Risk - don't send by road?

blocks.note: first meaning: to stake or endanger something
second meaning: dispatch goods by railway track instead

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning reads the idiom literally: the line is the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something on the line is to stake it, while literally it is loading freight onto a railway.

clue.text: Risk taking student into the choir

blocks.note: to chance something is to risk it
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A singing student taking a gamble on joining the church choir.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the eastern part of a church near the altar, where the choir stalls stand, so it is the choir in the architectural sense.

clue.text: He took his time (vulgarly), never mind anyone else

definitions.text: He took his time (vulgarly), never mind anyone else

indicators.note: in a coarse accent the opening aitch of words is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written, before the aitch goes
took, as in obtained
taken as written, before the aitch goes
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone helping himself at leisure without regard for others.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in an aitch-dropping accent, ''E got 'is t' becomes EGOTIST; the whole clue then describes such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: An egotist is self-centred, taking whatever he wants and caring nothing for other people.

clue.text: I'm good at location, whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: the word reads the same from either end, so either direction gives it

blocks.note: the system speaking of itself

explanation.surface: A boast from someone with a great sense of direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar systems detect and locate aircraft and ships by bouncing radio waves off them.

clue.text: Racing vehicle reversed into tree to get article of lambskin

indicators.note: the racing vehicle is read backwards
the turned vehicle goes inside the tree

blocks.note: a kart is a small racing car, as in go-karting
the ash is a common tree
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A go-kart crashes backwards into a tree, and the driver comes off with a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like an item of clothing, which suits a lambskin; it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrakhan is the tightly curled fleece of young karakul lambs, named after the Russian city.

clue.text: Attracted by knowledge and intelligence in cover-up

indicators.note: in a down clue the cover is read upwards, so backwards
the knowledge and intelligence go inside the cover

blocks.note: ken is range of knowledge, as in beyond my ken
wit is mental sharpness
a hat covers the head

explanation.surface: A spy drawn to an intelligence agency's cover-up operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover-up' looks like one word for concealment; it splits into cover and the signal up.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken with someone is to be charmed or captivated by them.

clue.text: Not in one's cabin, needing to be picked up?

blocks.note: first meaning: up on the open deck of a ship
second meaning: lying on the floor

explanation.walkthrough: The deck is both a ship's open floor and, informally, the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger outside the cabin is up top on board, and something dropped is lying at your feet.

clue.text: Cart whose base needs some protection from the rain

indicators.note: only some of the rain protection is used, its end dropped

blocks.note: whose base points back to this word: its bottom letter in a down entry
what you hold up in a shower

explanation.surface: A cart that needs shielding from the weather at its bottom end.
explanation.walkthrough: Cart is both the definition and, through 'whose base', the source of a letter: the bottom of a down entry is its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbrel was a two-wheeled farm cart, famous for carrying prisoners to the guillotine.

clue.text: Drug scene starts up - stay resolved

indicators.note: the opening letters of the word are taken
in a down clue the opening letters are read upwards, backwards
resolved in the sense of broken up and reformed

blocks.note: the first three letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party where drugs start appearing and someone firmly decides to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is the street name for the stimulant MDMA, a recreational drug.

clue.text: Hard to get your teeth into? Too bad!

definitions.text: Hard to get your teeth into

blocks.clueFragment: Hard to get your teeth into
blocks.note: first meaning: chewy, like overcooked meat
second meaning: an unsympathetic retort

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes the first part look like an invitation to a task; it is about chewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough meat resists chewing, and the word alone is a curt dismissal of someone's complaint.

clue.text: Little boy with great fear not ended by percussion

indicators.note: the fear is cut short, losing its final letter

blocks.note: Tiny Tim is the little boy in A Christmas Carol
panic is overwhelming fear

explanation.surface: A small boy whose terror never stops, caused by a din of drums.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are the kettledrums of an orchestra, part of its percussion section.

clue.text: Lift and bend to get commendation

blocks.note: a U-bend, shaped like the letter
praise is approval or commendation

explanation.surface: Instructions for an exercise class: lift, bend, and earn the instructor's approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To upraise is an old verb for raising something up, elevating it.

clue.text: Politicians in heaven preceded Edward VIII

indicators.note: the politicians are placed inside the heavenly city

blocks.note: MPs are Members of Parliament
Sion, or Zion, is the heavenly city in hymns

explanation.surface: Politicians gone to glory ahead of the king who abdicated.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallis Simpson came before the crown for Edward VIII, who abdicated in 1936 to marry her.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Simpson took precedence over the throne in the king's priorities, a witty sense of preceding him.

clue.text: Clouds not in my backiard?

blocks.note: the opening letters of these three words
read as back plus iard, a misspelt yard, giving their two initials

explanation.surface: A grumble about rain clouds over one's own garden.
explanation.walkthrough: NIMBY stands for not in my back yard; the setter misspells yard as iard so the initials end in I and give the plural of nimbus.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbi is a plural of nimbus, a dark rain-bearing cloud.

clue.text: Miners with real problem, anything from 1 to 9?

indicators.note: a word with a problem is in trouble, its letters disordered

blocks.note: the NUM is Britain's National Union of Mineworkers
taken as written

explanation.surface: Miners with a genuine grievance, asked to rate it on a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Each single digit 1 to 9 is a figure written as a symbol representing a number.

clue.text: Feet where hands should be under the masthead

blocks.note: a yard is three feet
hands belong at the end of the arm

explanation.surface: An order on a sailing ship: everyone's feet where the hands ought to be, below the top of the mast.
explanation.walkthrough: Hands are also sailors, which keeps the surface at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is either end of a spar slung across a mast, below its top.

clue.text: It could be the reverse of a fixer at first

indicators.note: the whole string that follows is read backwards

blocks.note: a nail fixes things together
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one, first

explanation.surface: A puzzled guess about what something is, perhaps a mechanic's back-to-front tool.
explanation.walkthrough: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it; NAIL + AT + I reversed spells ITALIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The drinks abbreviation It stands for Italian vermouth, so It is an example of the word.

clue.text: Risk a spirited stage production

blocks.note: first meaning: court danger
second meaning: a drama staged with fire

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning reads the idiom as a noun phrase: a play that has fire in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To play with fire is an idiom for taking dangerous chances, and fire means passion or spirit.
